title: Start/stop circuits and seal-in
summary: The motor start/stop circuit with a seal-in (self-holding) contact is the most important pattern in machine control. It turns two momentary buttons into a lasting run state with stop priority.

sections.heading: The pattern
sections.body:
A momentary Start button must start a motor that keeps running after the button is released. The output itself is used as a condition ("seal-in"):

```
MotorContactor := (StartPB OR MotorContactor) AND StopPB AND OverloadOK;
```

Read it as: *run if Start is pressed or we are already running, as long as Stop is not pressed and the overload relay is healthy.*

sections.heading: Stop priority
sections.body: Because the stop conditions are AND-ed after the OR, Stop always wins when both buttons are pressed. Reversing the order (`StartPB OR (MotorContactor AND StopPB)`) gives **start priority**, which is unacceptable for a motor.

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.body: The contactor's auxiliary contact (MotorFeedback) tells the PLC that the contactor really pulled in. Comparing command and feedback detects a failed contactor or a missing supply. In PLC Lab you can watch command, feedback and motor speed side by side in the Watch and Waveforms views.
